children.text: A flat coral island in the Visayan Sea off northwest Cebu, prized for Santa Fe's fine white sand, calm water, and fresh seafood. With little large-scale development, it feels unhurried, and a single motorbike is enough to tour the whole island at a leisurely pace.
Bantayan Island lies about
1 hour
by ferry from Hagnaya Port at the northwestern tip of the main island of Cebu. The whole island is a low, flat coral-limestone terrain, about
16km
north to south and about
11km

east to west, divided into three municipalities: Santa Fe, Bantayan, and Madridejos. Travelers mostly stay in Santa Fe in the southeast, where the ferry docks, with its stretches of flour-fine white sand such as Sugar Beach and Paradise Beach.

The island has long been known as the "Egg Basket of the Visayas" for its thriving poultry farming, and its specialties are danggit, sun-dried fish caught at sea, and dried squid. In Bantayan town on the west of the island stands the Church of Saints Peter and Paul, whose parish dates back to around
, making it one of the oldest parishes in the Philippines. In Madridejos to the north, the remains of a Spanish-era watchtower (a kota), built to guard against pirates, still stand.

Bantayan is especially crowded during Holy Week. Catholic tradition calls for abstaining from meat during Holy Week, but it's said that the Church granted Bantayan a dispensation because the island depends on fishing and poultry farming; during this period, vacationers flood in from all over Cebu and lodging books out months in advance. At other times the island is generally quiet with modest prices — not as flashy as Boracay, but well suited to families, couples, and long-term stayers looking to relax on a quiet beach.
The island took a direct hit from Typhoon Yolanda in
and suffered heavy damage, but most of it has since been restored. Coral reefs ring the island, keeping the water shallow and calm, which makes it good for swimming with children too.
The island covers about 108.8 km², a little over one-sixth the size of Seoul, and is so flat that its highest point reaches only

above sea level. The population is about 160,000, and each municipality has its own character. Santa Fe is the tourist hub, with the port, the airport, and beachfront resorts; Bantayan town is the central town, with egg production and the old church; and Madridejos is a village at the island's northern tip centered on dried-fish processing and fishing. Public transport is scarce, so the usual plan is to base yourself in Santa Fe and spend one day circling the island by motorbike. Even after the
September 30, 2025
northern Cebu earthquake, beachfront accommodations and ferries are mostly operating normally, but some places are closed off, such as the church and Ogtong Cave, so check the notes below.

blocks.title: Santa Fe's Sugar Beach and Paradise Beach

children.text: Beaches lining the southern coast of Santa Fe, with fine sand and shallow water good for swimming and sunbathing all afternoon. Paradise Beach charges a small entrance fee in exchange for fewer crowds and a quieter atmosphere.

Small islands offshore to the east, such as Virgin Island and Hilantagaan Island, are toured by bangka for snorkeling. Virgin Island is privately owned and charges a separate landing fee, and its policies sometimes change, so check before you go.
This is a popular spot for swimming in the clear groundwater pool of a limestone cave inside Ogtong Cave Resort in Santa Fe. However, falling rocks during the
September 30, 2025
earthquake led to the cave being closed for a safety inspection, and as of
it is still unclear whether it will reopen, so check with the resort before you go. Entrance to the resort's beach and pool is about
for adults and about
for children.
The Church of Saints Peter and Paul has an impressive, weighty facade built of coral stone, and on Good Friday night of Holy Week a procession of religious images winds along the plaza. However, the
September 30, 2025
earthquake broke the front gable and the cross at the top, so entry to the church is closed and Mass is held in the yard; check on the state of repairs before you visit.

Kota Park in Madridejos, at the island's northern tip, is where the remains of a Spanish-era stone fortress (the kota), built to guard against pirates, still face the sea, and there is a lighthouse nearby. Entry is generally free, and it is said to be the best place on the island to watch the sunset, so arrive about an hour before sundown. It takes about
30–45 minutes
by motorbike from Santa Fe, and it gets dark on the way back, so check your motorbike's headlight.

blocks.title: Riding a motorbike around the island

children.text: The ring road around the island is flat with little traffic, making it fairly easy even for motorbike beginners. In a single day you can see the scenery shift between rice paddies, poultry farms, fishing villages, and mangrove forests.
Danggit, dried squid, and dried shrimp can be bought cheaply at shops around Bantayan town market and near Santa Fe port. Many shops offer vacuum packing, which makes them good gifts.
A mangrove forest park in Obo-ob village, Bantayan town. Walk along a bamboo boardwalk about
1km
long and climb the observation tower at the end for a sweeping view of the forest and the sea. Admission is about
and the walk takes
30–45 minutes
; it is about
20–25 minutes
from Santa Fe by motorbike. Check opening hours and the fees for extras such as kayaking on site.

It takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB). Since
August 2024
, LEASCOR has operated a Mactan–Bantayan route (about
30 minutes
) to Bantayan Airport in Santa Fe (runway
). However, flights run only a few days a week, have been suspended temporarily because of fuel problems, and fares vary by report from
one way to several thousand pesos. Don't build your schedule around this flight; check with the airline or a travel agency first whether it is operating. The reliable way is by land and sea via Cebu.
From the North Bus Terminal next to SM City Cebu in Cebu City, Ceres buses bound for Hagnaya leave frequently from early in the morning. The trip takes about
3–4 hours
and the fare is about
. Hiring a van or Grab from Mactan Airport to Hagnaya takes about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
and costs about
. Some bus companies also sell combined bus-and-ferry tickets.
Island Shipping and Super Shuttle Ferry run several times a day from Hagnaya Port (San Remigio) to Santa Fe Port. The trip takes about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
, and the fare is about

, with a terminal fee charged separately. Tickets sell out easily during Holy Week and holidays, so we recommend booking online or arriving early. A small tourism or environmental fee is sometimes collected on arrival in Santa Fe.
The terminal fee at Hagnaya is about
, and an environmental fee of
is charged separately on arrival in Santa Fe. According to the operators, boats run from 2–3 AM until late afternoon, but the last boat (roughly
) varies by company and day of the week. Fares that rose because of fuel costs in
March
came back down from
May 11
and now run about
depending on the company.
The
September 30, 2025

northern Cebu earthquake caused part of Hagnaya Port to subside, so at high tide seawater covers part of the pier and the damaged area is closed off. The Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) restricts boarding and disembarking at high tide, so departures are often delayed by more than
1 hour
depending on the tide; from Cebu City, leave in the morning if possible, and leave slack against your flight time on the day you return.
Ceres Liner also offers direct services from Cebu's North Bus Terminal to Bantayan town and Madridejos, in which the bus itself is carried aboard the ferry. Fares are about
to Bantayan town and about
to Madridejos. There are no transfers, which is convenient, but reviews say departures are infrequent, so check departure times at the terminal counter first.
Aznar Shipping runs passenger and cargo-passenger vessels to Santa Fe from Cawit Port in Medellin, in northern Cebu. The trip takes about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
, and the regular fare is about
(non-air-conditioned) to

(air-conditioned). There are three or four sailings a day and the timetable differs by day of the week, so check the latest schedule; this route is presented as an alternative when the Hagnaya pier is congested or delayed by the tide.

a day, and a half-day tricycle tour is about
From Santa Fe it is about
10km
to Bantayan town (about
20 minutes
by motorbike) and about
30–45 minutes
to Kota Park in Madridejos. Shared tricycles from the port start at about
per person.
Bantayan is best during the dry season,
December–May
, and
March–May
, when the sea is calm and the sun is strong, is the peak of the beach season.
December–February
brings some wind from the northeast monsoon, but the cooler air makes it pleasant for touring by motorbike.
June–November
is the rainy season, with more showers and overcast days, and especially during
September–November
typhoons can cancel ferries on some days. Since the island itself is flat and low-lying, strong-wind damage during typhoons can be significant, so be sure to check the forecast.
Holy Week (
late March to mid-April
, varies by year) is the island's busiest period, with accommodation prices doubling or tripling and the beach filling with tent campers. If you want quiet, avoid Holy Week and the early
May
holidays. Conversely, if you want to experience the local festival atmosphere, this is the liveliest time to visit.
Daytime temperatures in the dry season are generally
. Festivals differ by municipality. In Bantayan town, the Palawod Festival around the feast day of the patron saints Peter and Paul on
June 29
is the biggest. Santa Fe holds the Panuhug Festival around the feast of the Santo Niño in
January
, and Madridejos holds the Isda Festival honoring fishing on the Feast of the Immaculate Conception on
December 8
. Dates and events change every year, so check the latest announcements.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Traveler accommodations are mostly clustered along the south coast, within
10 minutes
by tricycle of Santa Fe Port. Mid-range beachfront resorts run about
a night, and village guesthouses are around
. For somewhere quieter, small resorts on the north side of Santa Fe or the island's west coast are also good, but they have fewer restaurants and amenities, so renting a motorbike is convenient.

Seafood is undoubtedly Bantayan's signature food. At barbecue restaurants around the Santa Fe beach and Bantayan town market, you pick fish, squid, shrimp, and shellfish that are grilled and priced by weight — generally cheaper than in Cebu City. In the morning, be sure to try "danggit silog": fried dried danggit served with garlic rice and egg. Thanks to the island's poultry farms, eggs are fresh and cheap, and local egg dishes and leche flan are also popular.

By municipality, Santa Fe has resorts strung along Kota Beach and Sugar Beach, giving the best beach access, while Bantayan town and Madridejos have fewer places to stay but are cheaper and let you see local life up close. A meal at a local eatery (carinderia) is about
, and a main dish at a beachfront restaurant is about

. Sutukil is a combination of sugba (grilled), tuwa (soup), and kinilaw (raw fish cured in vinegar), and the kitchen cooks the fish you choose however you like. Dried-fish processing is centered in Madridejos and eggs in Bantayan town, and you can drink tuba, a palm wine made from coconut sap, all over the island.
The island has a few ATMs in Santa Fe and Bantayan town, but cash often runs out during Holy Week and weekends. Bring enough cash from Cebu.
Ferry tickets are sold one-way, and it's safer to buy your return ticket the day before during peak season too.
Since most beaches face southeast, sunrise is best seen from Santa Fe beach, and sunset from Bantayan town or Kota Park on the west side of the island.
Always wear a helmet when renting a motorbike. Even on provincial roads in the Philippines, helmet checks do happen.
Smart and Globe signal reaches most of the island, but data speeds can be slow on outlying beaches.
Shallow water also means the sea recedes far out at low tide, making swimming difficult. Check the tide schedule and plan beach time around high tide.

Dried fish may be subject to quarantine inspection when brought into countries such as Korea, so buy small amounts of vacuum-packed products and check the import rules of the country you are returning to.
The cheapest way to go island hopping is to pay the eco fee (about
per person) at the Santa Fe tourism office and be assigned a bangka. A boat is chartered for about
for five people, and the Virgin Island entrance fee varies by source, from
, so ask for the total before you set off.
At Bantayan church, do not disturb the Mass held in the yard, and do not cross the safety fence. The parish has asked visitors not to take fallen debris home as souvenirs.
If you have a flight home, it is safer to leave Bantayan and stay in Cebu City the day before, rather than traveling on the day of your flight.
During Holy Week, ferry waits can stretch to several hours and accommodations can all fill up. If you're going during this period, be sure to book your lodging and ferry in advance.
There are sea urchins and sharp coral scattered around the beach, so wear aqua shoes.
Life jackets are mandatory on island-hopping boats. Don't board a boat that doesn't provide one.
Midday UV is very strong and can burn skin in a short time. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard.
Ferries can be suspended for several days straight during typhoon season, so avoid staying on the island right up until your departure.
Local ordinances restrict littering on the beach and the use of plastic bags. Bring your own water bottle and shopping bag.

Fake booking sites and Facebook pages impersonating Bantayan accommodation are on the rise, and scams where only a deposit is collected before contact is cut off are occurring one after another. Book only after verifying the accommodation through a well-known booking platform or its official contact details, and be suspicious of requests to send money to a personal account or e-wallet.
About
40 minutes
by bangka from Maya Port at the northern tip of Cebu, an island world famous for thresher shark diving.
About
2 hours
by ferry from Danao Port in eastern Cebu, with Lake Danao and cave pools.
About
3–4 hours
by bus from Hagnaya, with Spanish-era landmarks such as Magellan's Cross and the Basilica del Santo Niño.
A sandbar island reached by bangka from Malapascua or Leyte, easy to combine with Bantayan for a northern Cebu island-hopping itinerary.
